_comment: SHARED TEST VECTOR for the UIFPE-149 slot arithmetic. Asserted by BOTH
module is the source of truth and the TypeScript copy exists only because
the wizard has to preview a table's run times; this file is what stops the
two from drifting into disagreeing about WHEN a pipeline runs.
Slot values are minutes since midnight UTC. Timestamps are UTC.
Every case here was chosen for a reason — see `why` on each.
gold-weekly (UIFPE-532) walks a 7-day grid of (weekday in weekly_days,
start_time) in UTC. previousSlot cases may carry `weekly_days`; when
absent the default ["MON"] applies. 2026-09-23 is a Wednesday.

slots.why: The canonical example. 8h from 06:30 tiles the day evenly because 480 divides 1440; the 22:30 -> 06:30 wrap is exactly 8h, not a short night.
A start time that is NOT itself the first slot of the day. 14:45 on a 4h interval phases to 02:45, and 14:45 must still appear.
Product's live daily schedule: exactly one slot, at 06:30.
6h from 06:30 phases to 00:30 — an interval that does not divide the start time.
The 8h default start time, which is deliberately staggered off :00.
The hourly rung on its historical :45 offset.
The finest rung, aligned to midnight: a full 288-slot day.
A start time in the last minutes of the day, phasing back to 00:20.
gold-weekly has at most ONE slot on a run day: the anchor itself. The day grid lives in previousSlot, not here.

previousSlot.why: BEFORE the day's first slot — the answer is YESTERDAY's last one. This is the case a naive implementation gets wrong by clamping to midnight, which would make a pipeline look due every tick until 06:30.
Exactly ON the slot. Must return that slot, so a run started at 06:30 is not considered due again.
One minute BEFORE the daily slot: still yesterday's. A tick that fires slightly early must not dispatch today's run early.
Seconds are truncated: 10:07:45 resolves to the 06:45 slot, not to 10:45.
Midnight exactly, on the finest rung.
Last minute of the day on the finest rung.
Crosses a YEAR boundary backwards. Month/year arithmetic must come from real date handling, not from subtracting a day.
Crosses a month boundary backwards, on a leap-adjacent month.
Weekly, default day set: no weekly_days given means Monday. Wednesday resolves to the Monday just gone.
Tue+Thu, mid-week: Wednesday afternoon resolves to Tuesday's slot, not to any interval arithmetic.
Tue+Thu, the long gap: Monday resolves to LAST Thursday, five days back. Uneven gaps need no interval.
Exactly on the Thursday slot: the slot is at-or-before now, so it is the current one (the tick at 03:00 dispatches).
One minute before the Thursday slot: still Tuesday's. An early tick must not pull Thursday's run forward.
Week boundary: a Sunday slot at 23:50 seen from Monday 00:05 is five minutes back, not a week.
Day tokens are case-insensitive and duplicates are harmless: ["thu", "THU", "tue"] is Tue+Thu.
